<margin>Already the proof of being exhausted by frugality.</margin>
<margin>Retreating is also regret.</margin>
<margin>Method of writing: Circle.</margin>
<margin>Not reaching.</margin>
<margin>Method of writing: Circle.</margin>
<margin>Always like this.</margin>
<margin>Not because one considers it proper to act, and thus acts; "fú" <gloss>to wear/to submit</gloss> is like the "fú" <gloss>to wear/to keep in mind</gloss> in "taking it to heart."</margin>
<margin>And if one contends with them again, then disaster will follow.</margin>
<margin>Method of phrasing: Circle.</margin>
<margin>What I practice.</margin>
<margin>Appearance of walking sideways.</margin>

Laozi's limitlessness being like drinking, the <term>Laozi</term> <gloss>Old Master</gloss> remained indifferent and did not respond. The next day, Shicheng Qi saw him again and said, 
<note>Discussion</note>
Formerly I found fault with you. Now my heart has changed and settled. Why is this? Laozi said, As for those who are clever, wise, or holy, I consider myself free from such things. Before, if you called me an ox, I accepted it as an ox. If you called me a horse, I accepted it as a horse. If one possesses the reality, and others give it a name, if one does not accept it, one will suffer disaster twice over. My "submission" is constant; I do not "submit" because I have something to submit to. Shicheng Qi held his actions in check, avoiding shadows and walking carefully.

<summary>This passage records an interaction between Laozi and Shicheng Qi, where Laozi explains his indifference to external labels and his philosophy of non-contention.</summary>
<keywords>Laozi, Shicheng Qi, non-contention, reality, names, philosophy</keywords>
